items.source: shipuniverse 24 Nov (warning numbers, times, IMOs, PGSA); Riviera 24 Nov (Ambrey, Equasis, 217-26 = GM 2 interception, Kelly quote); Tribune/ANI 24 Nov 16:47Z (UKMTO text; '2025 UTC' 'Sunday'); ABC live 24 Nov 14:03Z ('Monday evening'); marketcalls 25 Nov (UKMTO notice text, 22 Nov); CBS live 24 Nov (anchored-tanker fire)
items.note: late:true - incident dated 22 Nov 20:25Z per UKMTO's revised numbering (inside the previous gate window, within the 2-day tolerance) but first announced Tue 24 Nov and absent from the 11-23/11-24 files (grep 'Prosperity' / '219-26' empty); kept once. The IRGC's Monday 'three tankers under US air escort' claim (recorded 11-24) now has a UKMTO counterpart in COUNT (three VLCCs, eastbound = outbound, same evening) but NOT in cause (projectiles, not mines) or escort (no CENTCOM statement; Kelly: 'CENTCOM says the southern route is clear'). The date conflict (UKMTO 22 Nov vs press 23 Nov) is unresolved; if 22 Nov, the IRGC Monday claim post-dated the strikes by ~a day. No UKMTO/JMIC/CENTCOM primary page fetched. Three laden VLCCs (935k dwt combined) hit on the Omani-side lane is the largest single-evening tanker-strike set of the sequence; still 'continued transit, crew accounted for' - no sinking, no casualties printed.

items.name: Iranian mine claims 24-25 Nov vs confirmation: 2 new claim-events, 0 confirmed. (1) Tue 24 Nov: IRGC Navy (IRIB): one tanker 'earlier today struck a naval mine and exploded, catching fire east of the waterway', two others turned back after a radio warning from the Hormuz Traffic Control Centre ('Traveling through fake and unauthorized routes will result in nothing but explosions and fires for violators'); Iranian Army/Navy (IRIB, Tue morning): two tankers caught fire after entering a restricted area east of the strait with identification/navigation systems disabled ('tanker owners are required to coordinate with the armed forces for safe passage'; the waterway 'will never be reopened until Iran's objectives and demands are met'). (2) Wed 25 Nov early hours (The National): IRGC - 'two more tankers' exploded and caught fire on a 'false route' off the southern and eastern coasts ('Naval mines did not allow them to pass, causing massive explosions and fires'). Press totals: ANI/Tribune 'four' (Tue), Saxo 'four', Marine Insight 'five over two days', gCaptain 'four more... ten reported strikes'. Confirmed by any maritime authority: 0 (UKMTO: projectiles; Kelly: 'still no evidence of mines'; ABC: CENTCOM has called earlier IRGC mine claims false; no CENTCOM statement this window)
items.source: Tribune/ANI 24 Nov 16:47Z (IRGC + Navy PR texts); CBS live 24 Nov (navy statement); Gulf News live 24 Nov 13:24 GST (army two-tanker); The National 25 Nov 08:20Z (IRGC 'two more' Wed); Riviera 24 Nov (Fars/IRGC versions; 'a fourth tanker'); straits.live 25 Nov (IRNA/Saudi Gazette/gCaptain relays); Saxo 25 Nov
items.note: The IRGC and Army statements on Tuesday may describe the same hulls (one vs two tankers east of the strait) - counted as one Tuesday claim-event; the Wednesday 'two more' is a second. Cumulative hulls claimed since 21 Nov: 1 (Al Ghanam) + 2 (22 Nov) + 3 (23 Nov) + 2 (24 Nov, Army) + 2 (25 Nov) = ~10 claimed, 0 confirmed as mine strikes; UKMTO's three projectile strikes (219-221-26) are the only authority-confirmed hits in the same period. Pattern: Iran now claims a mine hit on roughly every day the US-facilitated lane carries traffic, and frames each as 'unauthorized route' enforcement - the claim rate itself is the M-panel reading.

items.name: Trump, NY Post Oval Office interview (Tue 24 Nov afternoon, published Tue): the Iran campaign is 'funded' 'up until really the end of January', when Democrats take Congress; 'We can put that war to bed anytime we want'; if Democrats cut funding 'they'll take a total win and make it a loss'; Israel's regime-change goal 'probably doable' but 'I was never for or against regime change, that was never a criteria for me'; on Iran's compensation demand: 'they killed 75,000 protesters in the last seven months'. NBC (Tue, unnamed officials): the administration is debating options including targeting/killing senior Iranian leaders - no decision; opponents warn it would strengthen hardliners. Democrats have discussed using spending bills to restrict offensive-operations funding (The National). US embassy Jerusalem security alert on Houthi attacks and Iranian efforts against US figures/facilities (Yedioth). No Vance/Rubio/Witkoff Iran statement dated 24-25 Nov beyond the Qatari MOFA readout of Monday's Rubio meeting ('regularly scheduled biannual', 'commitment to Qatar's security')
items.headline: Trump (NY Post, Tue 24 Nov): Iran war 'funded' through end-January, 'we can put that war to bed anytime we want', regime change 'probably doable' but never his criterion; NBC: leadership-targeting option under debate
items.source: ABC live 25 Nov (Trump entry ~04:00Z, 'conducted in the Oval Office on Tuesday afternoon'); New Arab 25 Nov 08:47Z; The National 25 Nov 08:20Z; CBS live 24 Nov (Qatari MOFA readout)
items.note: T1 (US side): the first explicit funding horizon - end-January - which is also the first time-bound constraint Trump has put on his own side of the standoff; paired with the 22 Nov 'inclined to resume strikes after the New Year' (recorded 11-23), the two statements bracket a January decision window. 'Put that war to bed anytime we want' reads as a deal-readiness signal in the same breath as the strike re-dating; no mention of the seven conditions, Hormuz sequencing or the AP 'Hormuz-for-limited-relief' proposal (11-24). The NBC leadership-targeting report is sourced and undecided - T4-adjacent, recorded here as context.

items.name: Mediator track, Tue 24 Nov: Qatar's Al Ansari (weekly briefing, Gulf News 21:43 GST): contacts continue 'to narrow' US-Iran differences, Doha keeps details confidential, the priorities are reopening Hormuz and a return to talks; Qatari MOFA on Monday's Rubio meeting: a 'regularly scheduled biannual meeting', Rubio 'reaffirmed the United States' commitment to Qatar's security' and thanked the Amir 'as a global mediator'; Tehran's answer stands: Ghalibaf (Fars, 10:50 GST) - no negotiations until the seven conditions are met (relayed list: lift the naval blockade on Iranian ports, ease sanctions, release frozen funds, end hostilities on all fronts, formally declare the war over), US threats 'desperation', a hostile US move could widen the conflict; Araghchi (13:10 GST): a US land blockade is 'virtually impossible'; Baghaei (04:53 GST): Qatar's charge d'affaires summoned over the Qatari-German statement, viewed with 'surprise and regret'; VP Aref (Wed): essential-goods stocks 'in good shape'. No Witkoff, Oman, Pakistan, Turkey or IAEA item dated in the window; Israel: Katz (KAN, 22:05 GST) 'Iran is in the process of developing chemical weapons... The State of Israel will not allow them to reach that capability'; ex-army chief: ~440 kg enriched uranium undestroyed, no 'direct and immediate threat' before a government forms
items.headline: Qatar: contacts continue to narrow differences (details confidential); Tehran: no talks until seven conditions met, Qatar summoned; Israel's Katz: Iran 'developing chemical weapons'
items.source: Gulf News live 24 Nov (Al Ansari 21:43; Ghalibaf 10:50; Araghchi 13:10; Baghaei 04:53; Katz 22:05; ex-army chief 07:43 GST); CBS live 24 Nov (Qatari MOFA); The National 25 Nov (Aref, Ghalibaf)
items.note: T3: the Qatari channel is alive but opaque ('narrowing', no content), while Tehran's public line is unchanged for a fourth day and it has downgraded Doha diplomatically (summons + 'unexpected' + 'surprise and regret'). The Katz chemical-weapons claim is a new Israeli casus-belli framing on the day NBC reports a leadership-targeting debate in Washington - T4-adjacent escalation pressure from the Israeli side against the allied brake recorded 11-24. Nothing moved on sequencing.

items.name: Maritime regime, 24-25 Nov: UKMTO announces three VLCCs struck by unknown projectiles within 17 minutes on the Omani-side eastbound lane (219-26/220-26/221-26; Sinokor-managed Bahrain/Cameroon/Romania Prosperity, all PGSA-blacklisted; crews safe, transits continued) - the first authority-confirmed multi-VLCC strike set, which the IRGC frames as mines defeating a US escort; Iran adds two more mine claims (Tue: one/two tankers east of the strait with AIS off; Wed early: 'two more' on a 'false route'), warns ships off 'unauthorized routes' (Ozmaei: 'not a place to test unauthorised routes and ignore maritime warnings'), and the navy says the strait 'will never be reopened until Iran's objectives and demands are met'; Army chief Hatami: the strait to become 'increasingly closed'; UKMTO 217-26 resolved as a US interception of the LPG tanker GM 2 (Riviera) - the blockade is being enforced by boarding, not fire; hormuz.now AIS crossings 2 on Tue (0 inbound), 7-day 7.3/day; IMF PortWatch 1 transit on 22 Nov; no US-facilitated lane count for 22-24 Nov; CENTCOM silent; Kelly: 'still no evidence of mines'; US Coast Guard says it thwarted all ~50 ship cyberattacks under investigation
items.headline: UKMTO confirms three Sinokor VLCCs struck by projectiles on the Omani lane; Iran claims mines on four-five tankers over two days; AIS crossings fall to 2; 217-26 was a US boarding of LPG tanker GM 2
items.source: shipuniverse 24 Nov; Riviera 24 Nov; Tribune/ANI 24 Nov; ABC live 24 Nov 14:03Z / 16:49Z; Gulf News live 24 Nov (Ozmaei 11:20, army 13:24); The National 25 Nov; hormuz.now 24 Nov 23:28Z; straits.live 24-25 Nov; Kotak 25 Nov (IRGC 'container vessel' line)
items.note: M-panel: two regimes now visibly collide on the same lane - the US-facilitated eastbound (outbound, laden) traffic took three projectile hits in one evening, and Iran claims the lane itself is mined. Whether the three VLCCs were in a US-escorted group is unprinted (IRGC says yes; CENTCOM says nothing). The GM 2 resolution removes the 'US struck an Iranian-oil tanker' hypothesis from 11-24 (analyst X-post) - the blockade's enforcement remains interdiction/boarding. The AIS count (2) is now almost meaningless as a flow measure; the orchestrator's transit input should weight the JMIC/NCAGS assisted-passage count when printed. Kotak's 'IRGC targeted a container vessel on an unauthorised route' (Iranian state media, 25 Nov) is a further unverified claim with no ship name.

items.name: Gulf fronts, 24-25 Nov - the Houthi-Saudi exchange reaches the Eastern Province: (a) Tue 24 Nov Houthi drones hit the PIF tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District (second hit on the tower in under a week, third on the district); 11 injured (SPA/civil defence: 2 Saudis + 9 residents - 2 Indians, 3 Nepalis, 4 Egyptians; Maritime Executive says 'all foreign nationals'); al-Maliki: 'a cowardly terrorist attack', deliberate targeting of civilians 'would be met with a firm response'; two drones downed Tue, one over the Eastern Province early Wed; UAE/Qatar/Bahrain/India condemn; UK sanctions the Houthis + 4 officials; (b) coalition orders Hodeidah port evacuated Tue and strikes its 'operational capabilities' overnight Tue-Wed plus targets in Saada and Amran (large fire at the port per AMK Mapping; no casualty figures); Houthi leaders order the evacuation of Saudi Red Sea ports and threaten counterstrikes; Yemen army says Houthis ~60 km from Aden; (c) early Wed 25 Nov: coalition says air defences 'intercepted and destroyed four drones in Ras Tanura' (Eastern Province); Houthi spokesman Saree claims an 'accurate and direct' drone strike on the Ras Tanura refinery (550 kb/d, ~16% of Saudi refining; adjoining terminal ~6.5 mb/d) that 'caused fires', plus Riyadh 'in three phases'; Reuters: NASA satellite imagery shows thick black smoke over ~600 km2 around the refinery; Maritime Executive: 'Saudi forces reported a drone strike at Ras Tanura', FIRMS heat sources near the complex; Aramco and the Saudi government communications office did not respond; the coalition 'did not say the refinery there had been struck'; no export, loading or refinery-operations impact reported in any fetched page; the 22 Nov Rabigh claim also remains unconfirmed
items.headline: Houthis hit Riyadh's PIF tower (11 injured), coalition strikes Hodeidah port; Wed: four drones intercepted 'in Ras Tanura', Houthis claim refinery fires, Reuters sees a 600 km2 smoke plume - no Saudi/Aramco confirmation
items.source: Maritime Executive 24 Nov 23:32 (Riyadh, Hodeidah, Ras Tanura report); Kuwait Times/KUNA 25 Nov 09:42Z (coalition statement, SPA casualties, Eastern Province drone); Al Jazeera/AFP 24 Nov 14:27; The National 25 Nov 12:00Z (Saree quotes, four drones 'in Ras Tanura', refinery data); Al-Monitor/Reuters 25 Nov (NASA imagery, no comment); Gulf News live 24 Nov (16:43-19:28 GST Riyadh; 18:48 Aden; 22:47 UAE); ABC live 24 Nov 14:11Z
items.note: T4: the Yemen front crossed from the Red Sea side (Rabigh, Yanbu, pipeline) to the Gulf export side (Ras Tanura, the largest terminal) within the window - a geographic escalation whether or not the refinery was hit. The orchestrator's 'confirmed damage to a Gulf oil facility' threshold is NOT met on fetched evidence: the only confirmations are interceptions (four drones) and satellite smoke; Saree's claim and the Maritime Executive line are unconfirmed by any Saudi statement. HARD-EVENT candidate if Aramco/Saudi energy ministry confirms a hit or a loading disruption - unconfirmed at this run. Ras Tanura's prior war history (Aramco shut it 2 Mar after Iranian drones; Houthi missile claim 27 Oct; loadings resumed late June after a ~four-month halt) means a confirmed hit would be the second shutdown risk of the war. No oil page fetched after ~12:00Z, so no price reaction recorded.
